name: Trash Talk
label: Deathwish
lede: Trash Talk started in Sacramento in 2005 and kept moving: Steve Albini mixed the second record, Keith Morris guested on a single, and Odd Future Records signed them in 2012. Through all of it the band ran its own label.

eras.title: Sacramento, in a hurry
eras.text: Trash Talk formed in Sacramento in 2005 and moved fast: a demo, a split, a first full-length and a spot on a Deathwish imprint within about two years. The sound was crossover thrash and hardcore played at skatepark speed.

years.h: A demo on Sell Our Souls starts the band
years.p: [[Lee Spielman|f183f98c-117b-445d-a836-f2c141174e92]] and [[Spencer Pollard|e0dfbf99-c4b6-4add-a4b6-42144402d5bf]] form Trash Talk in Sacramento in 2005. The demo comes out on Sell Our Souls Records the same year.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the band to 2005 in Sacramento, with Spielman on vocals and Pollard on bass and backing vocals. The first release was a self-titled 7-inch on Sell Our Souls.

years.h: Trash Talk and Steel Trap share a 7-inch
years.p: The Bay Area band Steel Trap takes the other side of the split, out on Spiderghost Pressgang. It is Trash Talk's second release in about a year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trash Talk (band) · The FADER · Metal Insider
years.h: Garrett Stevenson takes the guitar, and later the books
years.p: [[Garrett Stevenson|c136c559-192c-4874-a48e-ee91095bf1c1]] joins in 2007, the year of the debut album Walking Disease on Rumble Records.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Stevenson as a member from 2007. He went on to run the band's business side: The FADER called him the de facto manager, and Metal Insider's interview names him as the member who handles most Trash Talk Collective operations.

years.h: Deathwish's Malfunction imprint signs the band
years.p: Trash Talk lands on Malfunction, an imprint of Deathwish Inc., and records the Plagues EP.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Malfunction signing to 2007 and lists the Plagues EP in 2008. The band toured heavily with Cruel Hand in this stretch.

eras.title: An Albini mix and a label of their own
eras.text: After the Deathwish compilation, the band went to Chicago to record with Steve Albini, then started Trash Talk Collective to put out its own records. Friends of the band ran the label from then on.

years.h: Deathwish packages Plagues with Walking Disease
years.p: The 17-track compilation pairs the six-song Plagues 7-inch with the earlier album. Exclaim reviewed it on April 24, 2008.
years.xp: Exclaim's Keith Carman heard Cryptic Slaughter, D.R.I. and Discharge in it, plus a [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]-style edge, and called the production crisp.

years.cap: Lee Spielman crouched on the floor mid-song at Chain Reaction, 2009
years.h: Steve Albini mixes the self-titled LP at Electrical Audio
years.p: The band records in Chicago, and [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] mixes the album. It comes out on Trash Talk Collective, with a 250-copy European vinyl pressing on Reflections Records.
years.xp: Discogs credits the recording to Electrical Audio in Chicago, with Albini mixing and Nick Zampiello mastering at New Alliance East. Spielman later said working with a friend on the next record was far more relaxed than Albini's strict schedule.

years.big: "Releasing our own records is something that we have always wanted to do."
years.h: Off Deathwish, onto a label of their own
years.p: Lee Spielman told Metal Insider that is why the band starts Trash Talk Collective after leaving the Malfunction/Deathwish arrangement.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band left Deathwish Inc. to start the label. Stevenson handles most of its business, with friends helping while the band is on tour.

years.cap: Lee Spielman singing at the Mohawk, Austin, 2009
years.h: Keith Morris of Black Flag guests on "East of Eden"
years.p: Morris, who also sang for the Circle Jerks and OFF!, appears on the 7-inch, released by Trash Talk Collective.
years.xp: The single pairs "East of Eden" with "Son of a Bitch". The same year the band played a live session for BBC Radio 1, and the UK label Hassle Records put out the two-disc compilation Shame.

eras.title: Explode
eras.text: Eyes & Nines got them a name outside hardcore: a magazine cover, a Kerrang award and long tours across the UK, Europe and the US. The hip-hop crowd was paying attention too.

years.cap: Lee Spielman singing in the crowd at SXSW, Austin, March 2010
years.h: Joby J. Ford of The Bronx produces Eyes & Nines
years.p: Recorded at Big Game Lodge. Greg Hetson plays extra guitar and Matt Caughthran adds vocals on several songs.
years.xp:
The band announced the record in February through its blog and offered a pre-order with the "Explode" single and video. Wikipedia lists a digital release around May 18 and physical copies in June, and reports a Metacritic score of 83. Rock Sound gave it 10 out of 10 and Pitchfork 7.8.

The Icelandic volcano eruption in April cost the band tour dates, Spielman said.

years.h: Trash Talk land the cover of The FADER
years.p: That is how the magazine's October 2010 cover story describes the four members. A November feature, "Trash Talk Explode", follows.
years.xp:
The FADER said the label was run by Stevenson, and reported the band had just won Kerrang's award for Best International Newcomer.

Pollard and Stevenson told the magazine about being Black musicians in a hardcore band; Stevenson recounted a bouncer refusing him entry to his own sold-out show.

years.cap: A Trash Talk guitarist on the Hevy Fest main stage, August 7, 2010
years.h: Bikers gather in a Clearwater parking lot
years.p: At a Clearwater, Florida show a speaker gets damaged, the owner demands payment and bikers turn up in the parking lot.
years.xp: Thrasher's interview places this on an 85-day tour through the UK, Europe and the US with The Bronx, Iron Age, Cold World and Sick of It All. The band left without injury and without paying.

years.h: True Panther Sounds puts out the Awake 7-inch
years.p: The five-song EP is released October 11, 2011, a year after the band's FADER cover.

years.h: Trash Talk back Odd Future at the Roxy
years.p: On December 23, 2011 the band plays behind [[Odd Future|519336c2-f5a3-4137-a88e-58fecc604575]] in Los Angeles. NPR later used that line for them.
years.xp: Odd Future sometimes performed "Radicals" with Trash Talk backing them. The link came from touring: NPR reported the band toured with [[Tyler, the Creator|f6beac20-5dfe-4d1f-ae02-0b0a740aafd6]] and Action Bronson.

eras.title: The punks on Odd Future Records
eras.text: Odd Future Records signed them, and Trash Talk became the label's first non-hip-hop act. Two albums followed, then a drummer change that took in a former Mars Volta player.

years.cap: Odd Future, Lil Wayne and Trash Talk share a stage in Los Angeles, 2012
years.h: Odd Future Records signs its first non-hip-hop act
years.p: On May 30, 2012 Trash Talk joins [[Odd Future|519336c2-f5a3-4137-a88e-58fecc604575]]'s label. AllMusic and Wikipedia both call them the first signing from outside hip-hop.
years.xp: The move put a Sacramento hardcore band in front of an Odd Future crowd, and 119 then reached No. 15 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart, Wikipedia says.

years.h: 119 puts Tyler, the Creator and Hodgy on "Blossom & Burn"
years.p: [[Hodgy|76600f02-c090-4d15-8782-680cde16bd98]] and Tyler guest on track 6 of a 14-song, 22-minute album released October 9, 2012.
years.xp: "F.E.B.N." came out as a single with a video on August 30. 119 was the first Odd Future Records release without an Odd Future member. Pitchfork gave it 7.4, and NME and Under the Radar were positive.

years.h: A former Mars Volta drummer joins
years.p: Thomas Pridgen, formerly of The Mars Volta, is announced as the band's drummer on May 13, 2013. Drummer Sam Bosson is not mentioned.
years.xp: Metal Injection and Lambgoat reported the move; The PRP noted there was no word on what happened to Bosson. Last.fm's summary instead names Devan Bentley as drummer from November 2013, and Wikipedia's infobox gives Pridgen 2014, so the timeline of drummers is unclear.

years.cap: Lee Spielman on stage at The Observatory, Santa Ana, February 2014
years.h: Alchemist and King Krule turn up on No Peace
years.p: The 16-song, 28-minute album came out May 27, 2014. Alchemist produces "Amnesiatic" and "Reprieve"; King Krule appears on "Stackin' Skins".
years.xp: Consequence gave it a C+, calling it a short blast of classic hardcore with occasional hip-hop and electronic touches.

eras.title: Still going
eras.text: The band kept releasing records, and Squalor was the first time a producer shaped one from start to finish.

years.h: Two years after No Peace, the Tangle EP
years.p: The band's first release in two years comes out on its own label, Trash Talk Collective.

years.h: Band says the new album is done
years.p: On October 18, 2019 Trash Talk announces it has finished a record. The release that follows is the Squalor EP.

years.h: Kenny Beats' first band project is Squalor
years.p: The five-song EP came out June 5, 2020, with live drums and guitars.
years.xp: Stevenson told Louder that it was the first time the band worked with a producer who shaped the record throughout, not just engineered. Thomas Pridgen returned on drums to record it.

years.h: A Poe story gets a snowy short film scored with Squalor
years.p: "Something Wicked" reimagines Edgar Allan Poe's "William Wilson" in snowy middle America. It was released October 14, 2020.
years.xp: Louder called the short film brutal, bleak and perversely beautiful.
